task: Wire the verified hero/cover artwork from docs/hero-artwork-refresh.json into dist/games.json.
scope: 12 allow-listed catalogue entries: 8 heroArt pointers (halo, bo1, quake3, surf, diablo, dos-doom-dec-1993, dos-fallout, dos-theme-hospital) and 4 art replacements with artFit removed (skate, pes6, simpsons, dos-lemmings-1991). Three receipt records are explicitly NOT applied: dos-prince-of-persia-1990, dos-civilization, dos-the-need-for-speed-sep-1995.

inputs.receiptReadNote: The receipt was rewritten by the artwork worker while this job was starting (20587 -> 25162 bytes). The file was polled for 35s until size and mtime were stable, then re-read. All pointers applied here come from that corrected revision; its sha256 is recorded above so any later revision is detectable.

appliedHeroArt.caveat: Collection-level art (Halo: The Master Chief Collection); the standalone 2001 title has no separate Steam library asset.
Franchise-level art for Black Ops; the destination exposes Zombies maps that ship inside that title.
Counter-Strike art stands in for CS Surf: surf is a community movement mode with no published artwork of its own.
GOG store banner (1600x740), not a Steam library_hero: the 1996 original is not distributed on Steam.
Art comes from the DOOM + DOOM II bundle page; the bundle contains the exact 1993 release this entry launches.
GOG store banner (1600x740), not a Steam library_hero: the 1997 original is not on Steam.

appliedCoverArt.attribution: Official EA key art for Skate 3 (2010) — the original, explicitly not the 2025 "skate." reboot. Portrait EA master cropped to 16:9 by EA itself.
appliedCoverArt.caveat: Storefront key art, not a gameplay screenshot. artFit:contain is dropped so the card centre-crops the 1.78 frame instead of letterboxing it.

appliedCoverArt.attribution: Pro Evolution Soccer 6 (2006, Konami), PC-edition screenshot from the SPOnG gallery.
appliedCoverArt.caveat: Depicts the PC edition, not the recompiled browser build the catalogue launches, and is not evidence that runtime works. 640px clears the 460px cover floor but not the 1280px hero floor, so it is a cover only. At 1.33 in a 1.88 card window the card centre-crops the frame.

appliedCoverArt.attribution: The Simpsons: Hit & Run (2003, Radical Entertainment/Vivendi), GameGrin gallery screenshot.
appliedCoverArt.caveat: 640px clears the 460px cover floor but not the 1280px hero floor; cover only. At 1.33 in a 1.88 card window the card centre-crops the frame. A validated 1024x576 alternative exists at assets/refresh-simpsons-alt-cover.jpg and is deliberately not wired: the receipt maps the GameGrin shot as the cover.

appliedCoverArt.attribution: Exact-title Amiga screen of Lemmings (1991, DMA Design/Psygnosis).
appliedCoverArt.caveat: Native 320x200 — no HD claim is made and none is available: the 1991 original shipped at 320x200, is not carried on Steam or GOG, and no genuine higher-resolution media was found. 320x200 is below the 460px cover width floor used for catalogue cards and far below the 1280x400 hero floor, so the card upscales the frame. The pixels are also the Amiga release, while this entry launches the dos.zone DOS build: same title, different port.
appliedCoverArt.limitation: below the 460px cover floor and the 1280x400 hero floor (native 320x200) — recorded limitation, no HD source claimed

preserved.note: The 11 featured (slide) entries and their order, the 1 spotlight flag, the 38 sandbox-pending availability values, every field of every entry outside the 12 allow-listed ones, and the key order of the 12 edited entries are unchanged. Only heroArt/art pointers and the four artFit keys were touched.

executed: sha256 of each of the 12 applied assets on disk compared with the sha256 recorded in the receipt — all 12 match (asserted inside scripts/apply-hero-artwork.mjs, which aborts without writing on any mismatch).
dist/ + pointer resolution for every art and heroArt value across all 54 entries — all resolve to existing files.
Deep equality of every non-allow-listed entry against a pre-run snapshot, plus constant entry/featured/spotlight/availability counts, re-checked after the write — passed.
Guard that the three rejected assets are referenced by no art/heroArt pointer before and after the run — passed.
Idempotency: a second run produced a byte-identical dist/games.json (sha256 101ce41dbb04cd4263776a0558b2c6034e1a423ca3765e0ccc3e468c08ad9782 both times).

npm run check passed: '54 games: unique IDs, HTTPS URLs, requirements, audit evidence, artwork files verified.' (node --check dist/app.js, node --check dist/player.mjs, node scripts/check-catalog.mjs).
notExecuted: No image vision or human visual inspection of any file: the pixels were never looked at, so no claim is made that an image depicts the named game or edition.
No browser render check: nothing confirms how the new crops look in the hero slider or cards on a real viewport.
No re-fetch of any source URL in this step; HTTP status, content type and dimensions are carried from the receipt, while only the on-disk bytes were re-hashed here.
No framing, hosting, streaming or monetisation check: nothing here implies permission to frame or redistribute any destination or any of this artwork.

localContextNote: The worktree copy of dist/games.json already contained uncommitted work from other workers (16 further dos.* expansion entries, plus other files outside this task). None of it was modified: the applier only writes the 12 allow-listed entries and asserts that everything else is byte-identical to its pre-run state.
caveat: Byte-level validation proves a file is a real image of the stated format, dimensions and hash. It does not prove the image depicts the named game/edition, and it does not prove any right to host, frame, stream or monetise the destination. This task edited only dist/games.json plus its two own deliverables; the receipt docs/hero-artwork-refresh.json was read, not written.
